question: Can my clients see all their invoices in one place and pay several of them at once?
reference_answer: The customer portal is a page, hosted by Ledgerly, where one of your clients can see everything they owe you and everything they have paid. It is available on all plans.

question: How does Ledgerly decide which open invoice a bank deposit belongs to?
reference_answer: A bank feed brings your bank transactions into Ledgerly and suggests which invoice each deposit pays. It saves you from recording payments by hand.

question: I spotted a mistake in a bill that already went out. What can I still correct?
reference_answer: You can edit an invoice after sending it, but changes are limited so your client never sees numbers that quietly differ from what they agreed to. What you can change On a Sent or Overdue invoice with no payments, you can change: When you save, Ledgerly keeps the previous version in the invoice history and offers to send the client an updated copy.

question: If I stop working with a client who still owes me money, will they keep getting chased?
reference_answer: Archiving does not cancel anything that is already running. If the customer has Sent or Overdue invoices, those invoices keep their reminders and late fees.

question: Can invoice emails show my own company address as the sender instead of Ledgerly's? What do I have to configure with my DNS host?
reference_answer: By default, emails go out from `invoices@example.com` with your business name as the sender name and your reply-to address. On Pro and Enterprise, you can send from your own domain instead, such as `billing@yourcompany.example`.

question: What do I need before I can set up SAML single sign-on for my team?
reference_answer: Single sign-on (SSO) lets your team sign in to Ledgerly with their company identity instead of a separate password. It is available on Enterprise only.

question: A client paid on day 25 after the due date but I'm only recording it on day 40. Will they be charged extra penalty for those days?
reference_answer: The date received matters. If a client actually paid on day 25 past due but you record it on day 40, set the date received to day 25 and Ledgerly removes any fee added for the days after the payment.

question: A client paid more than they owed. Where does the extra money go and how do I use it on their next bill?
reference_answer: A credit balance is money you owe a customer that can be used against their future invoices. It is shown on the customer record and on their statement.

question: What happens to late fees and the pay link when I void an invoice?
reference_answer: Voiding cancels an invoice that was already sent while keeping a record of it. The invoice stays in your history with the status Void, and its number is never reused.

question: How can I swap the credential my script uses for a new one without any outage?
reference_answer: Revoke a key Choose **Revoke** next to the key. It stops working immediately and cannot be restored.

question: What should I double-check when adding my first client so their invoices actually reach them?
reference_answer: You need a customer before you can invoice anyone. This quick start covers the minimum.

question: How can I stop my team from accidentally sending tiny invoices?
reference_answer: A minimum invoice amount stops you, or your team, from sending an invoice whose total is below a number you choose. It is useful if processing a very small invoice costs you more than it earns.

question: I'm brand new and just want to get a first bill together as fast as possible. What are the steps?
reference_answer: This quick start creates a simple invoice with one line. The full reference, including all the options, is in Create an invoice.

question: A client overpaid by mistake and wants the extra back as money. How do I return it?
reference_answer: A credit balance can be returned to the customer. If the credit came from a card payment made within 90 days, refund it through the payment (see Refunds).

question: Which settings are hardest to change later, so I should get them right from the start?
reference_answer: Add a customer and create your first invoice (see Add your first customer). Not sure about a setting?
